custom_tooltip: Fill in width and height to make the Custom option appear in the paper list.
duplex_tooltip: Duplex makes one file alternating fronts and backs. Single-sided splits fronts and backs into two files.
folding_instructions_title: How to fold quarto and octavo
folding_p1: Folding these two layouts is slightly more complex than the simple single-fold folio. Both of these have been designed so that the first fold is parallel to the short edge of the paper - eg, if you hold the page in portrait orientation, you will be folding the top edge to the bottom. One side of the page will have consecutive numbers across this fold (ie, 3 and 30 on the top row, 2 and 31). Fold inward across this line (so that 3 has been folded to lay against 2, and 30 against 31). The next fold is along the other paper axis (parallel to the original long edge). For quarto, you want to find the side with the numbers closest together, and fold inwards to match them (this will be consecutive on the innermost sheet). For octavo, look at the bottom-most row and find the consecutive pair, then fold inward. Octavo has one last fold, for which you want to find the pair remaning that are closest, and fold them together.
folding_p2_1: Or, if you want to just memorize the order, once you find the first fold side, the order is:
folding_p2_quarto: quarto - top to bottom, fold points away from you, left to right, fold points towards you.
folding_p2_octavo: octavo - top to bottom, fold points away from you, left to right, fold points away from you, top to bottom, fold points towards you.
white_space_help: Relative to the original document. 1 pt = 1/72 in.
bounds_tooltip: Marks the PDF top and bottom on each signature’s outer folio.
sig_order_tooltip: Staggered lines show the signature sequence.
calc_sig_lengths_title: How sheets per signature are counted
calc_sig_lengths_p: A signature’s length is the number of full sheets of paper in it. In a folio, each sheet has one fold, so you punch through as many folds as there are sheets. In quarto, each sheet has two folds; in octavo, four; in sextodecimo, eight. Size your signatures with that in mind (you almost certainly want just one sheet for sextodecimo).
wacky_warn: Each printed sheet becomes one or more little books. Only the paper, printing and page options apply.
inst_1_3rd_p1: Cut along the lines or cut just extra bit off the top (along exposed 'top' of page) and then fold up along the dotted lines (if trimming, you can just trim off the cruft at the bottom-- tops need to be even for leveling purposes however). Outer margins intentionally under-marked so you can trim wherever feels right after folding & assembly.
inst_1_3rd_p2: Not the most paper efficient of layouts, but it's optimized for organization (if a signature is just one page, harder to botch the ordering) and many, smaller signatures make for rounder backs and large swell in my [six's] opinion (which helps w/ nice shoulders, if you're into that sort of thing)
inst_a7: Cut the vertical center line. You can also cut the horizontal lines if you like, or just fold it up as detailed above.
sig_8_zine_small: 8 per side, printed on one side, no cutting
inst_8_zine: The classic no-cut, single page zine! Just fold it up right and you've got yourself a mutant non-standard folio making an 8 page little fellow-- all extra pages beyond 8 are discarded. For better folding instructions than I could possibly write, see:
landscape_warn: Landscape layout: print flipping on the short edge.
test_print_warn: Remember to do a single-sheet test print if it's your first time to make sure duplex/mirroring is correct!
inst_a3_p1: Cut out the rows. Fold up the folios like a zig-zag (two per face). Then fold the center of the text (smoosh the two matching page numbers together).
fold_center_warn: Note that when folding, it's important for the center of the folios to line up. That's what I measure against (less so fretting about folding exactly at the edge). Remember! Printer skew is a real thing!
inst_a9: Cut along the cut lines. Fold up the 3 folio signatures, then the 4 folio.
inst_a4_p1: Cut out the rows. Fold up the folios like a zig-zag (two per face). Then fold the center of the text (smoosh the two matching page numbers together).
sig_a10_small: 60 per side, 6 rows of 2 and 3-folio signatures
inst_a10_p1: Thankfully most small layouts fit on one page-- easy enough to do a test print and make sure you're duplexing correctly (if that's your route)
inst_a10_p2: Cut out the rows. Fold up the folios like a big zig-zag (two per face). Then fold the first 2 folios into a signature and the last 3 folios into a signature. I often cut them apart only when I'm stitching things together.
flyleafs_tooltip: Blank sheets at the start and end of the book.
btn_preview_tooltip: No preview with “Signature files only”; single-sided printing shows one side only.
btn_reset_tooltip: Your settings are saved in this browser and in the URL. This resets everything.
privacy_note: Your PDF never leaves your computer
drop_sub: Pick a format in the settings and download the imposition ready to print.
download_note: You get a .zip with the print-ready files.
booklet_desc: One signature folded in half. Great for zines and staples.
custom_sig_desc: You set how many sheets go in each signature.
perfectbound_desc: Loose sheets glued at the spine.
alternate_page_rotation_hint: Alternates page rotation between front and back.
sewing_img_alt: Sewing diagram: A is the margin, B the number of stations, C the tape width. A 0 pt tape makes a single dot.
file_error: That file didn’t open as a PDF. Try another file.
generate_error: Couldn’t generate the files. Check the options and try again.
preview_error: Couldn’t build the preview. Check the options and try again.
page_range_syntax: Use numbers and hyphens, like 1-8 or 1,3,5-7. All pages are used for now.
page_range_out_of_range: That range is outside the PDF. All pages are used for now.
credit: This app is a fork of bookbinder-js, created by momijizukamori and contributors from the original Bookbinder. All of the imposition logic comes from their work.
out_settings_link: Made with Miolo. To make it again with the same settings, open:
presets_empty: Save the settings you use most to switch formats in one click.
sheet_lead: {n} pages per side of a {paper} sheet.
sheet_lead_one: One page per side of a {paper} sheet.
sheet_scale_same: Each page goes in at actual size.
sheet_scale_warning: Check the scale: 10 pt text in the PDF prints at {size} pt.
zine_page_warning: The zine uses only the first 8 of the {total} pages.
preview_first_signature: Preview of signature 1 of {total}, front and back.
preview_first_sheet: Preview of sheet 1 of {total}, front and back.
custom_sig_syntax: Use whole numbers separated by commas, like 10, 10, 8.
custom_sig_short: These signatures add up to {sum} sheets, but the pages fill {needed}: the end of the book is left out.
custom_sig_long: These signatures add up to {sum} sheets and the pages fill {needed}; the rest prints blank at the end.
print_actual_size: Print at actual size (100%), with “fit to page” turned off.
print_duplex: Print just the first sheet, front and back, and check it: if the back comes out upside down, switch the flip edge on the printer (long or short edge).
print_single: Print the fronts file, put the stack back in the tray, and print the backs file. Test with the first sheet first.
fold_times: Fold each sheet in half {n} times (see “How to fold quarto and octavo”)
gather_signatures: {fold} and nest the sheets into signatures of {n}, in order.
gather_custom: {fold} and nest the sheets into the signatures you set ({list}), in order.
gather_booklet: {fold} and nest all the sheets inside one another; sew or staple along the fold.
gather_perfect: {fold}, stack the sheets in order and glue along the spine.
gather_single_sheet: To fold and cut, follow the layout’s instructions under Binding → Single sheet.
